correctness.rationale: A vertex in the last zero-block has neighborhood exactly the final one-block, forcing at least \(k\) selections there. Any selected vertex in a kTDS needs \(k\) distinct selected neighbors, so the set has size at least \(k+1\). Conversely every earlier vertex is adjacent to every final-block vertex, an unselected final-block vertex is universal, and a selected final-block vertex sees all other selected vertices; the two inequalities are therefore sufficient. The polynomial subtracts only the size-\(k\) subsets wholly inside the final block, and every larger feasible set contains a feasible size-\(k+1\) subset. Fresh literal replay checked 167,480 cases through order eight.

value.rationale: The result upgrades optimization-only threshold coverage to a complete feasible-family theorem for every multiplicity, yields every coefficient and every inclusion-minimal set, and proves a striking profile collapse: all earlier creation blocks are forgotten once \(N\) and the final universal block size are fixed. That is a natural structural fact for a standard domination parameter.

final_claim: For a connected threshold graph with final \(1\)-block of size \(b\), a set is \(k\)-tuple total dominating exactly when it contains at least \(k\) vertices of that final block and has at least \(k+1\) vertices in total; hence the stated polynomial, inclusion-minimal-set count, and profile collapse to \((N,b,k)\) hold.
limitations: Only connected threshold graphs and uniform open-neighborhood requirements are covered; nonuniform vector domination is outside the claim.
